title: Archive router for unresolved Blaschka market and deaccession chains
purpose: Route auction/provenance gaps to specific archival series and record identifiers instead of repeating low-yield generic web searches.

priority_targets.research_problem: Identify the five unnamed institutional recipients and distinguish institutional transfer from private-market disposal in the 1925-1927 Blaschka deaccession.
priority_targets.record_title: Nominal File: Arrangements, Transfer and Disposal of Exhibits - Index, 1913 to 1960
priority_targets.status: identifier recovered in project provenance backend; public web indexing does not expose the index contents
priority_targets.why_first: The project backend has already identified the 1920-1927 transfer/disposal composite. The long-run index is the shortest route to the relevant nominal-file numbers, subject headings and recipient institutions before ordering a large composite file.
expected_yield: possible distinction between transfer and sale/private disposal

priority_targets.research_problem: Recover the actual 1925-1927 Blaschka transfer/disposal paperwork after routing through the index.
priority_targets.record_title_raw: Nominal File: Arrangements, Transfer and Disposal of Exhibits - parts 11/1 to 101/3, 1920 to 1927
priority_targets.identifier_title_conflict: The public identifier in the project archive audit terminates at 101/2 while the displayed title describes parts through 101/3. Preserve both raw strings until the archive confirms the hierarchy.
priority_targets.status: exact target identified; contents not publicly indexed
priority_targets.use_rule: Inspect only the portions identified from CORP/SCM/02/02/7/421 rather than scanning the entire composite blindly.

priority_targets.research_problem: Trace ultimate disposal for exact Science Museum numbers, including the three later Christie's objects.

publicly_verified_child.title: Museum Store Register nos. 1- 3687. These vols. record objects in a running number sequence, with notes on store location and ultimate disposal

priority_targets.why_high_value: The official catalogue explicitly says the registers contain notes on store location and ultimate disposal. Exact historical Science Museum identifiers from Cardiff and Christie's can therefore act as anchors even if transfer correspondence omits the maker name.
priority_targets.access_note: Official catalogue states material is available to researchers through the relevant Science Museum Group archive centre.

priority_targets.research_problem: Bridge the 1877 registration cohort to later store/disposal records.
priority_targets.record_title: Rough copy of entries in Register of Science Library, relating to objects exhibited in the Western Galleries and the Educational Division, with explanatory notes
priority_targets.why_high_value: Its starting year coincides with the 1877 Blaschka registration cohort and it may expose historical numbers or explanatory notes that can be matched to later disposal records.
priority_targets.guard: The catalogue title establishes chronological and administrative relevance, not that Blaschka entries are present.

priority_targets.institution: Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Zoologische Lehrsammlung / historical Zoologisches Institut
priority_targets.research_problem: Test whether Krefeld 2025 lots 26-27, both labelled Zoolog. Institut Universität, Berlin, can be identified in the HU teaching-collection inventory or in its documented dispersal history.
priority_targets.current_public_proof: HU's collections portal exposes multiple surviving Blaschka teaching models dated 1885 and 1887 and also preserves the exact institutional label formula Zoolog. Institut/ Universität Berlin on other teaching objects.

high_value_event.description: HU records a decision to reduce the teaching collection; parts were given away, many specimens were lost, and other parts were transferred to the Museum für Naturkunde.
high_value_event.status: documented collection-level dispersal window; no Krefeld object bridge yet

search_targets: historical Zoologisches Institut / Lehrsammlung inventory books
old inventory numbers and taxon names for anemone/polyp models
priority_targets.guard: Do not infer that either lot left in 1970. The event is a provenance hypothesis window until an object-level record is recovered.

priority_targets.institution: Museum für Naturkunde Berlin, Historical Division
priority_targets.research_problem: Crosswalk Krefeld 2025 lots 26-27 and any HU transfer candidates against the separate MfN historical Blaschka inventory.
priority_targets.runtime_status: link resolved from archived institutional page; PDF body not fetched in current research runtime
priority_targets.relationship_to_hu: Keep MfN separate from HU. HU records that some teaching-collection material was transferred to MfN during the 1970 reduction, but this does not prove either Krefeld lot followed that route.
priority_targets.dating_conflict: Krefeld catalogues both objects around 1870; current HU Blaschka examples recovered publicly are dated 1885 or 1887. Preserve the auction dates until an object-level crosswalk resolves the chronology.

priority_targets.research_problem: Close the 1904 Mason sale notice -> 1909 Glasgow institutional purchase chain while preserving the auction-layer exclusion.
target_records: Mason estate correspondence and collection list
known_facts: December 1904 Museums Journal notice advertised 300 Blaschka invertebrate models from the Mason estate.
Corning Museum of Glass states Mrs Mason sold Mason's Blaschka models to Glasgow Museums in 1909 for GBP 275.
Exact 1909 quantity remains unresolved; 300 must remain the advertised 1904 quantity.
priority_targets.policy_effect: The 1909 event remains outside the canonical auction lot count because the buyer is an explicitly identified municipal museum.

priority_targets.institution: unknown English public school / unnamed London dealer
priority_targets.research_problem: Identify the dispersed educational Blaschka collection that supplied part of George Loudon's holdings.
priority_targets.known_evidence: George Loudon says he found Blaschkas with a London dealer and was told they came from a public school quietly disposing of them; his Corning account describes several dealer purchases and says the school had closed its natural-history department for financial reasons.
search_targets: English public-school natural-history department closures/disposal notices
local auction catalogues after school disposal
priority_targets.guard: Dealer testimony establishes a market route, not a public auction and not the school identity.

order: Science Museum transfer/disposal index before generic recipient search
HU teaching-collection/dispersal records before treating Berlin as a single collection
exact historical number before generic maker name
known prior institution before broad auction-house search
institutional acquisition stays outside canonical auction count
strategy.rationale: Generic Blaschka and glass-model auction searches have reached sharply diminishing returns. The remaining high-value gaps are archival routing, institutional branch separation and object-number crosswalk problems.
